rounds.text: Khyati Multimedia Entertainment Ltd is currently trading at a significant discount relative to its sector, with a P/E ratio of 17.47x compared to the benchmark of 38.04x [E6]. This valuation gap is further underscored by a P/B ratio of 2.49x, which sits well below the sector benchmark of 6.68x [E7]. The company has demonstrated a powerful operational turnaround, evidenced by a current ROE of 15.9% [E13] and a 16% median ROE over the last year [E28]. This performance stands in stark contrast to the sector’s negative ROE benchmark of -53.9% [E9] and the company's own superior ROA of 5.44% against a negative sector benchmark of -2.15% [E8]. Conceded: the company has a history of poor long-term profitability, with median ROE figures of -6%, -10%, and -13% over the last 10, 5, and 3 years respectively [E25, E26, E27, E59]. Conceded: the company currently offers no dividend yield to shareholders [E4]. Despite these historical challenges, the recent shift toward positive, sector-beating returns suggests the market has yet to fully price in the company's improved financial efficiency [E8, E9, E13, E28].

The bull’s reliance on recent ROE figures [E13, E28] ignores the overwhelming weight of long-term evidence showing a persistent pattern of value destruction. While the bull highlights a single year of positive performance, the median ROE over 10, 5, and 3 years remains deeply negative at -6%, -10%, and -13% respectively [E25, E26, E27]. This structural inability to generate consistent returns is explicitly flagged as a negative for the company [E59], casting significant doubt on whether the recent uptick is a sustainable turnaround or merely a temporary anomaly. Furthermore, the bull’s focus on valuation multiples [E6, E7] fails to account for the fact that the company provides zero dividend yield to shareholders [E4], offering no tangible return for the risk of holding such a small-cap entity [E3]. Conceded: the company currently maintains a higher ROE and ROA than the provided sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E13]. Ultimately, the recent improvement in profitability is statistically outweighed by a decade of poor performance, suggesting that the current valuation may be a reflection of long-term skepticism rather than an overlooked opportunity.
